hypothesis: A mandatory real 10-14 minute turn plan bound to WORKING authority is sufficient to keep a worker productive for most of the quarter window.
learning: Plan validity is necessary but not sufficient. The worker can finish declared substeps and still cease durable progress far before the intended window.
do_not_repeat_without_new_evidence: Adding more plan prose or more detailed substeps alone.

hypothesis: Separate runtime continuity from scheduler delivery and measure continuous evidence rather than sparse endpoints.
learning: The invocation can remain substantively productive for >12 minutes, but fixed-window 840 seconds is mathematically impossible when delivery+startup consumes >60 seconds. Runtime longevity and scheduler budget are independent constraints.
next: Use hard continuation authority for voluntary-yield control while pursuing event/independent wake architecture for jitter tolerance.

hypothesis: Machine-readable denial of voluntary yield during nonterminal ownership, plus a feasible scheduler budget, can prevent objective-complete early return and approach 840 evidenced seconds.
learning: The hard continuation gate supports long healthy execution but cannot physically prevent the ChatGPT invocation from ending. Treat pre-final denial as behavioral protection only; independent wake latency is a separate hard requirement.
next: Measure and reduce abrupt-boundary recovery gap rather than adding more no-yield prose.

hypothesis: Separating behavioral no-yield from physical recovery and measuring cold-rescue latency will localize the remaining utilization bottleneck.
learning: The fixed-quarter canonical was a valid recovery mechanism but far too slow for the recovery SLO. Policy hardening alone cannot close this gap.
next: Prioritize a genuinely independent event wake; keep Actions as best-effort rescue.

hypothesis: Rolling same-canonical hourly RRULE lifecycle can remove fixed-quarter normal continuation loss while retaining bounded cold rescue.
learning: The canary generalized to production for normal completion-relative reentry. Normal continuation and abrupt-loss recovery are distinct: the former now has a ~64s production scheduler-delay sample, while abrupt loss can still wait for the ~780s provisional rescue horizon plus jitter.
next: Collect and audit three rolling 900s useful-coverage windows; independently provision an event wake path for <=120s abrupt-loss recovery.

hypothesis: Removing retired scheduler semantics from cold-start policy surfaces and adding a strict promotion contract will prevent control drift and false-positive rolling utilization acceptance.
learning: The scheduler-control ambiguity is removed at source, but exact evidence still exposes a 790-second unexplained cross-run gap. The correct response is rejection/INCOMPLETE, not endpoint-span inference. Further policy prose is not the utilization bottleneck.
do_not_repeat_without_new_evidence: Additional scheduler wording cleanup as a substitute for runtime/wake improvement.
next: Use strict promotion rules for subsequent samples and shift expected-effect priority toward runtime/wake mechanisms that can reduce observed cross-run gaps; preserve same-canonical rolling continuation meanwhile.

hypothesis: Separating rolling scheduler delivery delay, startup overhead, active-invocation useful span, and abrupt-loss recovery will identify the dominant remaining P0 loss and prevent obsolete fixed-quarter baselines from distorting event-wake decisions.
change: Align event-wake fallback and promotion baseline to SAME_CANONICAL_ROLLING_RRULE; collect exact final-rearm, observed-wake, first-substantive-work and last-substantive-progress timestamps without endpoint inference.
success_signal: At least one complete rolling observation with cause-separated latency fields and no internal substantive gap >120s; then repeat toward three accepted windows.
do_not_repeat_without_new_evidence: Policy-only scheduler wording cleanup or comparison against retired fixed-quarter cadence.
next: Collect exact epoch-26 substantive evidence and final-rearm/next-wake boundaries; if abrupt runtime loss dominates, independent event consumer remains the highest-value upgrade.
